They examine how AI-generated papers may distort academic incentives and warn against outsourcing thinking entirely. The central concern: ensuring humans continue developing their reasoning abilities as AI handles more intellectual tasks.

title: 首部AI长剧《后西游记》，带飞A股影视板块涨停潮
content: China's first full-process AIGC long-form drama "Journey to the West II" premiered on Hunan TV and Mango TV on August 31, 2026, triggering a stock surge in A/V media companies. The 30-episode mythological series was produced in just five months using AI technology, significantly cutting costs and production time. It marks two milestones: first AIGC long drama on satellite TV prime time, and first implementation of "produce-review-broadcast simultaneously" model under China's "Broadcasting 21" policy, enabling episode-by-episode iteration based on audience feedback. Mango Super Media's stock hit two consecutive 20% daily limits. The drama, adapted from a 17th-century novel about the Monkey King's successor, has received mixed reviews but demonstrates AI's potential to restructure entertainment industry production models. The case signals that future AI entertainment competition will center on storytelling quality and cultural depth rather than technical spectacle alone.

title: 紫金与神华：两种世界观的对决
content:
Zijin Mining and Shenhua Energy represent two fundamentally different investment philosophies. Zijin bets on commodity prices, using its acquisition and operational expertise to profit from copper, gold, and lithium price cycles. Its "capability moat" enables global expansion but requires continuous validation. Shenhua relies on institutional protections—long-term coal contracts and integrated infrastructure—that create an irreplicable, state-backed monopoly. Its "resource moat" offers stability but limited growth.

The market values Shenhua at 20x PE versus Zijin's 17x, preferring apparent stability. Yet Shenhua faces long-term demand decline from decarbonization policies, while Zijin's resource scarcity provides enduring value. Zijin's returns show convexity—unlimited upside with protected downside; Shenhua's are linear, like a high-yield bond. The optimal approach combines both: Zijin for offense, Shenhua for defense, exploiting their low correlation.

title: 不写代码的人做技术产品，最后卡在哪？
content: Non-coders building tech products with AI tools face a fundamental verification gap. While product skills like defining requirements, breaking down workflows, and setting acceptance criteria help manage AI coding assistants, pre-change impact assessment remains impossible. The AI can summarize affected files, but users cannot verify completeness—hidden dependencies slip through until tests fail or things break. All safeguards are reactive: small commits, isolated changes, rollbacks. True proactive validation is missing, and learning to code wouldn't fully solve it, since AI-generated codebases are too large to manually audit.

title: 全新OpenClaw 2.0发布：龙虾史上最大更新，已无人关心
content:
OpenClaw 2.0 launched after seven weeks of silence with 933 contributors and 16,000 PRs—half the project's total history. The update came too late; most users had already left after Anthropic closed an OAuth loophole in April 2026 that let users exploit $20 subscriptions for thousands in API value, causing some bills to spike 50x. Founder Peter Steinberger departed for OpenAI in February.

The article argues OpenClaw pioneered the "Harness" architecture—tool scheduling, permissions, and execution layers around AI models—now standard across the industry. However, competitors captured every niche: Claude Code and Codex dominate coding; Feishu's CLI owns China's enterprise market with native API integration; and standardized alternatives like Goose, MCP, and AGENTS.md emerged under the Linux Foundation. OpenClaw's security failures, delayed fixes, and "life assistant" model with poor productivity returns sealed its decline.

title: 这两个月，我被一个免费 AI 模型反复震惊
content: The author describes being repeatedly surprised by a free Chinese AI model's capabilities in programming assistance. Over two months, the AI helped build: a blog API with WebMCP protocol integration; an offline snapshot of a closing mahjong game including protocol reverse-engineering and a game engine; a POSIX-compatible static site generator running in WASM Linux; and numerous terminal blog features including WebRTC P2P networking and VLESS gateway. The author primarily provided requirements while the AI wrote code.
